welcome.heading: Welcome to Garden State Strikers
welcome.lead: We are glad you found us. While our roots began as a casual neighborhood gathering, today we are a tight-knit, closed group of passionate cricketers across New Jersey who come together every weekend for three to four hours of high-energy, spirited cricket.
welcome.storyCtaText: Want to see how it all began? Read our club story below.
welcome.philosophy: The moment we step onto the field, job titles, backgrounds, and everyday distractions stay at the boundary line we play strictly as one team. Respecting teammates, honoring the spirit of the game, and genuinely celebrating each other’s success always come first. We believe that when camaraderie and grit lead the way, winning naturally follows.
welcome.connect: If those values sound like how you love to play the game, we would love to connect. Reach out and let’s see how we can share the pitch together.

history.heading: Our History
history.subheading: From a father-and-son playground pitch in New Providence to USCL & Millennium Twenty20 contenders across New Jersey
history.intro: Every great club is built on persistence, principle, and a love for the game that refuses to be sidelined. Here is how Garden State Strikers came to life.

chapters.title: A Father, a Son, and a Playground Pitch
chapters.description: Our story began in the summer of 2020 in the small town of New Providence, New Jersey. Founding member Chethan Raghavendra who grew up in a family of disciplined athletes and represented his state at the age-group level headed out to the open playground at Allen Roberts Elementary School with his son, Pushan Raghavendra, to stay active. With cricket in their DNA, it wasn’t long before bat and ball came out. Their daily father-son sessions quickly caught the eye of neighbors, and within a few weeks, a casual backyard workout had snowballed into a full squad playing every single weekday after work.

chapters.title: Scouting Grounds with a Measuring Tape
chapters.description: Seeing the enthusiasm across town, Chethan, Pushan, and fellow founding members set their sights on building a permanent home for local cricket. Because cricket is still a niche sport in the U.S., getting field space wasn’t easy. Chethan and Pushan drove to every park in town with a measuring tape to find underutilized spaces where a cricket pitch could coexist without disrupting existing sports. After days of scouting, they pinpointed two neglected fields with real potential and rallied local residents to petition the township.

chapters.title: Turning a "No" into a Registered Club
chapters.description: As expected, the initial proposal was turned down. But persistence is woven into how we play we don’t walk away when the odds are stacked against us. The group requested an in-person meeting with the township councilman to walk through how cricket could safely share space with other community sports. The pitch worked. To secure field access, the township required an officially registered sports organization giving birth to our original club (which we’ll refer to as NPCC). Recognizing the talent in our ranks, we entered our very first New Jersey tournament in the USCL league.

chapters.title: The Birth of Garden State Strikers
chapters.founderHighlight: Chethan & Pushan Raghavendra • Keeping the Founding Spirit Alive
chapters.description:
As the saying goes, once the cake is baked, everyone wants a slice even those who never helped in the kitchen. By late 2022, internal politics crept in from individuals more interested in control than respecting teammates or the integrity of the game. Rather than compromise the culture we built from scratch, the core group made the principled decision to walk away and start fresh.

At the end of 2022, Garden State Strikers was born carrying forward the true spirit, camaraderie, and grit of the original founders. Today, the Strikers compete actively across the local New Jersey circuit, growing stronger in bond and roster every single season.

Even to this day, Chethan remains actively involved in preserving the core intent of the club and supporting the team wherever needed, while Pushan continues to contribute whenever time permits—stepping in as our official scorer during league games and cheering the team on every step of the way.

items.title: 5 Consecutive Postseason Campaigns Across USCL & Millennium Cricket League
items.description: After competing in USCL through Fall 2024 (highlighted by our 2024 USCL Summer T-20 Runner-Up finish), Garden State Strikers transitioned to the Millennium Cricket League finishing as 2026 Summer Gold Division Runner-Up (10W-2L-1NR) and going unbeaten in the 2026 MCL Fall T20 Elite regular season (5W-1L-1NR).

timelineTabs.label: Summer T20
timelineTabs.subtitle: USCL (2023–2024) & Millennium Cricket League Gold Division (2026) Summer T20 Campaigns

items.title: Inaugural GSS USCL Summer Playoff Run (8W – 5L – 1NR)
items.description: In our debut summer under the Garden State Strikers banner, GSS went 8-3-1 in regular-season play highlighted by posting 225/3 to beat United CC by 13 runs (Jun 18) and bowling out United CC for 77 (Jul 22) and Kings XI for 65 (Aug 12) to reach the Qualifier & Eliminator playoffs. Santosh Lalan led with 381 runs (HS 103) and 15 wickets.

items.title: USCL Summer T-20 Championship Finalists (9W – 2L – 2NR)
items.description: Posted an unbeaten 8-0-2 regular season in USCL Summer T-20 including a 160-run demolition of Edison Tigers (216/6 vs 56/10 on Jul 14) and defeated Nalwa The Great Warrior by 6 wickets in the Eliminator (140/4 vs 137/10 on Aug 4) to finish as 2024 USCL Runner-Up. Powered by Anbumani Mailathipathy (431 runs, HS 158, Avg 61.57) and Santosh Lalan (30 wickets, BBF 5/5, Econ 4.48).

items.title: Millennium Twenty20 Gold Division Runner-Up (10W – 2L – 1NR)
items.description: Opened the 2026 Gold Division campaign with a record 252/7 at Cedar Brook Park (145-run win vs NJ Revenants), reeled off a 7-0 start to finish 2nd in Group B (90% win rate), and skittled #1 seed Mumbai Gymkhana for 60 in Qualifier 1 (71-run win) to reach the Championship Final led by Prabakaran Jayabalan (470 runs, 5 fifties) and Santosh Lalan (15 wkts).

timelineTabs.label: Fall T20
timelineTabs.subtitle: 2024 USCL Fall T-20 & 2026 Millennium Cricket League (MCL Elite) Fall T20 Campaigns

items.title: USCL Fall T-20 Winning Finish (3W – 2L – 1NR)
items.description: Bowled out Edison Tigers for 112 (chasing 118/1 in 11.1 overs for a 9-wicket win on Sep 15), restricted Daredevils to 125/7 (chasing 126/5 in 17 overs for a 5-wicket win on Oct 6), and closed our final USCL season on a winning streak against Bergen Tigers CC paced by Prashant Madhukar (93 runs) and Asif Mohammed (5 wkts, Econ 2.86).

items.title: 2026 MCL Fall T20   MCL Elite Unbeaten Regular Season & Quarter Finalists (5W – 1L – 1NR)
items.description: Roared through the 2026 Millennium Cricket League (MCL Elite) Fall T20 regular season unbeaten (5W-0L-1NR) opening with a 111-run rout of Canopus CC (186/3 vs 75/10), edging Rebels CC by 14 runs, defending 113 in a 3-run thriller vs Mumbai Gymkhana, and defeating Wolverines and Jersey Bulls (by 26 runs) before a nail-biting 1-wicket Quarter Final finish against Mumbai Gymkhana (123 vs 124/9).

clauses.heading: 1. Club Nature & Membership
clauses.body: Garden State Strikers (GSS) is a private, closed recreational cricket club based in New Jersey. Access to this Progressive Web App (PWA) and website is provided for informational purposes for team members, alumni, league officials, and invited supporters. Participation in club practices, net sessions, and league fixtures is strictly by invitation and subject to adherence to our team code of conduct and spirit-of-the-game principles.

clauses.heading: 2. Intellectual Property & Club Identity
clauses.body: The Garden State Strikers name, shield crest, custom graphics, and written club history are the property of Garden State Strikers. You may not reproduce or use the club crest or branding for commercial purposes, merchandise, or unauthorized representation without prior written consent via info@gardenstatestrikers.org.

clauses.heading: 3. Accuracy of Match & Statistical Data
clauses.body: All match scores, seasonal timelines, and player career statistics are compiled from official league scorecards hosted on CricClubs (including USCL and Millennium Cricket League). While we strive to keep records accurate, official league portals remain the authoritative record for tournament standings and statistics.

clauses.heading: 1. Zero Personal Data Collection or Tracking
clauses.body: This website and Progressive Web App operate on a 100% static, serverless architecture. We do not use tracking cookies, advertising pixels, third-party analytics trackers, user login databases, or background telemetry. Your browsing activity on this app is never tracked, profiled, or sold.

clauses.heading: 2. Local Device Storage & Offline Cache
clauses.body: To provide a fast, native-like experience at cricket grounds with weak cellular reception, your browser stores a local copy of the app shell, roster JSON data, and your Light/Dark mode theme preference ('gss-theme' in localStorage) directly on your device. You may clear this local cache at any time through your browser settings.

clauses.heading: 3. Public Roster & Third-Party Links
clauses.body: Player names, roles, photos, and cricket statistics displayed in the Squad and History views reflect publicly published league participation records on CricClubs. Clicking external links (such as CricClubs scorecards, Apple/Google Maps directions, or social media deep links) will take you to third-party services governed by their own respective privacy policies. To request an update or removal of your profile photo or roster information, contact info@gardenstatestrikers.org.

clauses.heading: 1. Recreational Sport & Assumption of Risk
clauses.body: Hard-ball (leather-ball) cricket involves inherent physical risks. All players, guests, and visitors participating in or attending Garden State Strikers matches, net practices, or events at Cedar Brook Park or other league venues do so voluntarily and at their own risk. Garden State Strikers, its founders, captains, and members assume no liability for personal injury, property damage, or loss incurred during matches, practices, or travel.

clauses.heading: 2. Matchday Photography & Media Consent
clauses.body: Photographs and match highlights featured in the Gallery and Player Spotlight sections capture public league fixtures and club events. If you appear in any club photo and wish to have it credited, updated, or removed, please email info@gardenstatestrikers.org and we will promptly accommodate your request.

clauses.heading: 3. Non-Commercial Recreational Club
clauses.body: Garden State Strikers operates strictly as a community and recreational sporting group. This site does not process payments, sell tickets, or conduct commercial e-commerce transactions.
